Introduction

Texas licenses Personal Assistance Services (PAS) Agencies under the Home and Community Support Services Agency (HCSSA) framework. The TX Health & Human Services Commission (HHSC) — HCSSA Licensing Unit oversees licensing.

Table of Contents

  • Understand Texas’s Regulations
  • Choose the Type and Size of Agency
  • Business Structure and Licensing
  • Develop a Comprehensive Business Plan
  • Establish Operations Infrastructure
  • Hire and Train Qualified Staff
  • Policies, Procedures, and Care Plans
  • Marketing and Community Outreach
  • Maintain Compliance and Prepare for Inspections
  • Frequently Asked Questions

1. Understand Texas’s Regulations

HHSC licenses PAS agencies under Texas Health and Safety Code Chapter 142. Requirements include HCSSA licensing, background checks, training, and quality standards.

2. Choose the Type and Size of Agency

PAS agencies provide personal care, homemaker, companion, and attendant services.

3. Business Structure and Licensing

Register with the TX Secretary of State, apply for HCSSA license with PAS category, complete administrator certification, and secure insurance.

4. Develop a Comprehensive Business Plan

Texas benchmarks: Private pay rates $18-$28/hour, Medicaid attendant rates $14-$20/hour, break-even 12-18 months. Texas is the largest market by population.

5. Establish Operations Infrastructure

Set up office, scheduling, EVV systems, and documentation tools.

6. Hire and Train Qualified Staff

TX requires background checks and training per HCSSA standards.

7. Policies, Procedures, and Care Plans

Develop policies meeting HHSC requirements.

8. Marketing and Community Outreach

Build networks in Houston, Dallas-Fort Worth, San Antonio, Austin, and statewide.

9. Maintain Compliance and Prepare for Inspections

Maintain HCSSA licensing, EVV compliance, and quality programs.

10. Frequently Asked Questions

What is HCSSA? Home and Community Support Services Agency — the Texas licensing framework for home care providers.
